comments.text:
The inherent problem to getting over race in democratic systems is that while we're all human every race and culture while having the same needs also has different wants as well as values. While fractions of people from different demographics can certainly be integrated into a larger homogeneous society (and we should) the fact is on a large scale this doesn't work. What happens when you begin bringing in a different people with a different culture this creates friction. They have to agree to submit to the original culture but more often then not they refuse to acknowledge their culture is incorrect or incompatible (in-out group dynamics). 

A good example is the various religious laws of Islam. Such a child marriage, honor killings, FGM, anti-LGBTQ stances, and anti-free speech/blasphemy enforcement. In the west which has been created from Libertarian & Christian values which are directly opposed to these things. The two cultures simply cannot coexist because they are mutually exclusive of each other.

The other factor is a combination of low-IQ individuals who legally can't be held to the same legal standards because our laws recognize they can't actually understand the law. Which creates a two tiered justice system. Which means they are effectively free to commit crimes against others which is morally indefensible. To tribal cultures based around low trust societies where the focus is on providing for you, your family, and your tribe regardless if it's a direct detriment to someone else. In a capitalist system two groups (individuals or otherwise) would come together to figure out how they could both benefit and trade. In a tribal society it's not about benefiting both parties but your party only.

We see this in cultures outside the US especially in the "third world" where there's rampant government corruption that often evolves into totalitarianism, authoritarianism, or despotism. The issue with "moving past race" is that the one common factor across all these systems is that human fallibility component. All of these people have a different view on how to make their system work and often allow it to happen. It's why you've seen such a decay in various parts of Africa after the end of colonialism. These countries are destroying themselves through tribalism resulting in genocides and regional instability where for a time there was growth and progress when they were all forced together under one banner and vision.

Because at the end of the day Andrew Wilson is right in that you can only achieve your political and cultural goals through force. In a democracy where majority rules you can only keep exerting your vision of the world while your in the majority. Once you become the minority someone else's worldview takes precedence and you better hope that worldview doesn't involve the systematic erasure of your people which is a very common theme throughout history.

Ignoring this basic fundamental reality about the human condition when applied to social and cultural issues is one of the core problems in American politics right now.

I'm from Chicago and Tim is right - the "LeClare Courts" er what democrats portray as "affordable housing" was a housing project on the south side of 47th street, and North of 47th Street was a totally normal neighborhood but south of 47th - it was seriously a pile of rubble - it's one of the most bizarre things I've ever seen, but that's how it goes in Chicago... I mean objectively NO hyperbole - one side of the street looks like a bomb hit it, and the other side of the street is clean and normal - no garbage on the ground - none of that jazz... It always reminded me of "Alice in Wonderland" where one side Alice is in the forest and there is a distinct barrier between the dark and spooky side of the forest and the normal side - it's a significant difference - it just goes from "normal" to ultra-ghetto and all that divides the two is a street, just like that..

Also, I remember when Tim went to Sweden - that was back in the day when he would ride his skateboard through the streets of New York and talk about current events... It's crazy to think Tim went from that to what he's doing now and all the success he's had with all of the shows and stuff.. But I was following Tim since the beginning at OWS and he's pretty much the only reason why I never started a youtube channel - because I wanted to bring attention to the issues the media ignored at the time, but Tim started doing that so I never had to, and I'm totally fine with that just as long as people are aware of the issues.. And the funniest part is Time was a "reluctant" democrat for years - like he wanted to be a democrat so bad, but he saw the truth, he saw the reality and he didn't go down that path like so many people do so I have deep respect for the guy.. Although I'll admit - back in the OWS days I did NOT like him at all because I thought he was ANTIFA given the way he dresses, lol.. At the time I thought he was far too sympathetic to Antifa and I felt he was trying to portray them as the "good guys"...
